node.title: Re^3: open file using variable passed by form
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
length param('newCOMMENT')

This avoids warnings when param returns undef (at least on Perl 5.12 and up).

As for the regexes, have a look at [doc://perlrequick] and [doc://perlretut]. Using them, I make sure that param('event') contains only "word" characters (which excludes things like dots, slashes, or backslashes), and I make sure that newCOMMENT includes only "word" characters and horizontal whitespace (which excludes, for example, newlines; see [doc://perlrebackslash] and [doc://perlrecharclass] for all the details). I then use capture groups to "untaint" the values (see [doc://perlsec]). You may find that the regexes are too restrictive, in which case you can add allowed characters, but be very careful with this - adding too many or the wrong ones will open the security holes again. This is another good reason to not use form input for filenames and use a database instead, where these things are not an issue if you use the right tools - see [http://bobby-tables.com|Bobby Tables].
